text:
mike: Quick follow-up from the paged/blocked KV RFC thread. I ran a small bench on the mixed-chat workload and hit a few compatibility gotchas between the blocked KV layout and the attention kernel's assumptions.

mike: TL;DR: fragmentation + eviction compaction is causing either extra copies (to present contiguous KV to the kernel) or kernel falls back to a slow scattered path. Numbers: ~12% P50 latency regression for short context (<=512) when eviction churn > 30%/min.

sara: ouch. do you have the benchmark job id? how deterministic is the regression? :thinking:

mike: job 452 on perf-cluster. CI run reproduced it 3/3. Root cause looks like: our attention kernel expects contiguous KV memory per layer for the fused matmul+kv read kernels. Blocked cache uses page frames that can be non-contiguous after eviction/compaction. Kernel currently does memcpy -> contiguous buffer, run kernel, free. That copy is the perf hit when churn is high.

jin: two quick options: 1) make the kernel accept scatter-gather (iovec) and do gather loads inside kernels, or 2) adapt the cache to expose contiguous views (background compaction / pin hot ranges). each has tradeoffs.

oliver: +1. also consider a hybrid: kernel supports a fast-path for 1-2 iovecs and falls back to full copy if >N fragments. might get most wins.

mike: exactly. prototype notes:
```
# example cache config we used
kv.cache.eviction:
  policy: lru_segment
  segment_size: 65536  # 64kb frames
  max_frag_ratio: 0.25  # allow up to 25% of memory as fragmented tails
  compact_on_evict: false
```

mike: With compact_on_evict=false we avoid synchronous compaction but pay more fragments -> more memcpy. With true we pay compaction latency at eviction time (GC-like).

sara: what's the memory overhead of keeping both a fragmented and a compacted representation? e.g., pinning a compacted shadow copy for hot prefixes.

jin: shadow copies double memory for that region while pinned. But we can evict older shadow copies or use a cheap dedup path when fragments align. Alternatively, kernels that support scatter-gather can DMA-direct from multiple pages without copies on some hw (if we implement an iovec path). That reduces memory but increases kernel complexity and scheduling overhead.

oliver: hardware scatter-gather is nice but not universal across our fleet (older GPUs and some TPUs). We need a graceful fallback plan. Also need to update the kernel selection logic: currently we pick kernel based on model+seq len distribution; we should also include "fragment_count" and "churn_rate" signals.

mike: proposal: three-prong approach (short term -> long term):
- short: add kernel fallback that accepts up to 2 iovecs (fast-path) and memcpy for >2. cheap to implement, covers most cases.
- medium: add background async compaction job in the cache manager that coalesces adjacent frames during low load. configurable (max_bytes/sec).
- long: define cache metadata contract: per-page contiguous_run_id + frag_index so kernels can request a contiguous view or a scatter list. update runtime kernel selector to include fragment heuristics.

sara: sounds reasonable. for medium, can we avoid stalling inference threads? async compaction must not block pin/unpin APIs. we should expose backpressure markers in the cache API.

jin: implementation notes for the sg kernel: I can prototype microkernel that accepts up to 4 iovecs, uses local register-blocking gather, and returns to caller. benchmark on A100 shows ~6% regression vs pure contiguous for 2 iovecs, but much better than full memcpy in high-churn cases. will open a draft PR.

mike: thanks. action items: @jin prototype sg-kernel (2/4 iovecs) + perf numbers, @sara run job 452 variant with compact_on_evict=true to compare end-to-end p50/p95 and cost, @oliver update kernel selector RFC with fragment/churn heuristics. I'll draft a short compatibility doc describing the new page metadata fields.

oliver: I'll add a note to the runtime API: "cache pages MAY expose contiguous_run_id (string) and frag_index (int). Kernels SHOULD attempt iovec path before copy if supported." keep it as opt-in for now.

sara: ci-bot: can you re-run job 452 with compact_on_evict=true and cc results here? :pray:

ci-bot: Re-run queued: perf-cluster job 452 (variant compact-on-evict). started 2026-03-20T18:02:13Z. Will post artifacts when complete.

mike: one more thought: fragmentation also interacts with quantized layouts. when pages are quantized we may need to maintain alignment for vectorized loads. compaction must be quant-aware or we risk misaligned quant blocks. add to doc.

jin: good catch. I'll include quant-block boundaries in compaction heuristics.

oliver: risk matrix:
- risk: kernel complexity -> longer maintenance, harder testing. mitigation: limit iovec count and keep clear fallback.
- risk: compaction thrashes under sustained churn -> mitigation: rate-limit compaction, evict-old-first heuristics.
- risk: cross-hardware behavior divergence -> mitigation: selector + explicit per-region capability flags.

mike: that's it for now. If no objections I'll spin up the draft RFC addendum and link PRs once @jin has a prototype. thanks. :thumbsup:

sara: SG kernel sounds like the right short-term win. +1.

jin: on it, I'll post a WIP PR later today.

ci-bot: Benchmark artifacts uploaded: gs://redwood-perf/job452/variants/compact-true and /sg-kernel-proto. See logs for memcpy vs iovec timings.

oliver: thanks everyone. I'll track RFC updates in the architecture tracker.
